Glossary

Glossary of philosophical terms

52 terms that the archive's quotations use in a technical sense, in the language they came from.

49 of the 52 entries carry a specific misreading: a translation that hardened into a false equivalence and now circulates as though it were the text.

The archive's quotations are English renderings of Greek, Chinese, Sanskrit, Arabic, Hebrew, German, and French. Transliteration alone cannot carry that, so each entry names the original alongside the gloss.

How to use this glossary

Reach for an entry when a quotation uses a word you suspect is doing more work than its English equivalent admits. Each page gives what the term does in the argument it belongs to, what it is commonly mistranslated as, and where in the archive it is in play. The terms are not a dictionary: they are the words a reader of this corpus actually trips over.

Ancient Greek

  • aretē ἀρετή — excellence, the fulfilment of a thing's own standard
  • eudaimonia εὐδαιμονία — living well and doing well; human flourishing
  • phronēsis φρόνησις — practical wisdom; sound judgement about what to do
  • akrasia ἀκρασία — acting against one's own better judgement
  • elenchus ἔλεγχος — cross-examination; refutation by question and answer
  • aporia ἀπορία — impasse; the state of being unable to proceed either way
  • epistēmē and doxa ἐπιστήμη / δόξα — knowledge and opinion
  • telos τέλος — end, completion, the point of a thing
  • logos λόγος — account, reason, speech, proportion
  • nous νοῦς — intellect; direct apprehension
  • ataraxia ἀταραξία — undisturbedness; freedom from disturbance
  • epochē ἐποχή — suspension of judgement
  • prohairesis προαίρεσις — the faculty of choice; what is up to us
  • oikeiōsis οἰκείωσις — appropriation; coming to recognise something as one's own
  • katharsis κάθαρσις — purgation, cleansing

Latin

  • a priori / a posteriori — from what is prior / from what is subsequent
  • conatus — striving; the effort to persist in being
  • sub specie aeternitatis — under the aspect of eternity
  • amor fati — love of fate
  • ordo amoris — the order of loves
  • esse and essentia — existence and essence
  • habitus — a settled state; a durable disposition
  • intellectus and ratio — intellective apprehension and discursive reason
  • res cogitans / res extensa — thinking substance and extended substance

Chinese (pinyin)

  • dao 道 — way, path, course
  • de 德 — virtue, power, the efficacy a thing has by being what it is
  • wu wei 無為 — non-coercive action; acting without forcing
  • ziran 自然 — self-so; what is so of itself
  • ren 仁 — humaneness; being fully responsive to others as persons
  • li (principle 理) and li (ritual 禮) 理 / 禮 — two entirely distinct concepts that English renders identically
  • qi 氣 — the stuff and its dynamic configurations
  • xin and xing 心 / 性 — the heart-mind, and the nature one is born with
  • ming 命 — mandate, decree, what is allotted
  • cheng 誠 — sincerity, truthfulness, the completion of a thing's own nature
  • zhongyong 中庸 — equilibrium and constancy; not the mean between extremes
  • junzi 君子 — the noble person, literally 'son of a lord'

Sanskrit

  • ātman आत्मन् — self, breath, the innermost principle of a person
  • brahman ब्रह्मन् — the ground and totality of what is
  • māyā माया — power of appearance; the tendency of the world to seem self-standing
  • karma कर्मन् — action, and the residue action leaves
  • śūnyatā शून्यता — emptiness; absence of own-being
  • niṣkāma karma निष्काम कर्म — action without craving for its fruit

Sanskrit / Pali

  • dharma धर्म — the order that sustains things; also one's own duty; also a teaching
  • anātman / anattā — not-self; the absence of a permanent self

Japanese

  • satori 悟り — awakening; the direct seeing a practitioner works toward

Japanese / Chinese

  • mu 無 — the syllable of the first koan; no / nothing / without

Arabic

  • tawḥīd توحيد — affirming oneness; the unity of God
  • ijtihād اجتهاد — exerting oneself to derive a ruling; independent legal reasoning

Hebrew

  • teshuvah תְּשׁוּבָה — return; repentance
  • tikkun olam תִּקּוּן עוֹלָם — repairing the world

Nguni Bantu

  • ubuntu — the quality of being a person; humaneness

French (as used in African philosophy)

  • vital force (force vitale) — a putatively African concept of being as life-force
